note: The fuzz input supplies zero-delimited command-line arguments, here enabling --replay-gain and adding an invalid first filename before the generated temporary WAV input file.
The input-controlled --replay-gain option requests ReplayGain analysis during encoding.
The invalid first filename makes encode_file fail while the loop still carries the first-file state to the next filename in vulnerable revisions.
The safety obligation is that first must remain true unless the first encode_file call succeeded, because it controls ReplayGain initialization for the first successfully encoded file.
The temporary WAV file is encoded with is_first_file false, so grabbag__replaygain_init is skipped even though ReplayGain analysis is enabled.
ReplayGain analysis consumes the WAV samples while the ReplayGain stage has not been initialized, producing MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value.
